text:
Rasmus Andersson has spent most of his career in Calgary and is now 45 games into his time in Vegas. It hasn't clicked yet: 6 points in 18 games, and the Golden Knights take only 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, almost nine points worse than without him.

Some of that is luck. Vegas has scored 6.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Andersson out there, which has cost him points. And his own shooting (2 goals on 2.04 expected) is right on schedule. Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among 215 defensemen last season, most of it from even-strength offense, so the offensive game should come.

His minutes are rising, up nearly two a game over his last ten, including 24:30 in the loss to New Jersey. That suggests Vegas trusts him more than the on-ice numbers do. His skating is better than people assume, 85th percentile top speed. We project about 36 points. The thing to watch is whether the shot share climbs as he gets used to his partners. If it doesn't by Christmas, it becomes a real question.
headline: Rasmus Andersson, still settling
